content:
maia: heads-up — got a customer escalation from AcmeProd about a sharp p95/p99 regression on requests that use function/tool calling with structured JSON outputs. They started seeing timeouts and retries around 11:03 UTC. Our metrics show p95 from ~120ms -> 210ms and p99 spikes to 720ms for that route. request id: req_0ab12c.

ops-bot: Alert: latency_anomaly detected for route /v1/functions/router (team: acme-prod). window=5m, p99=720ms, p95=210ms, threshold=300ms.

jon: looking now — can you paste an example request payload and the headers (esp x-request-id and model+router versions)?

maia: sure — minimal repro from the customer: 
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/functions/route \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-..." \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -H "x-request-id: req_0ab12c" \\n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4-open","input":"Extract fields","tool_schema": {"type":"json","schema": {"type":"object","properties": {"items": {"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"},"meta":{"type":"object","properties":{"score":{"type":"number"}}}}}}}},"call": {"name":"extractor"}}'
```
They also attached a logfile showing repeated `validation.time_ms` spikes around 150-400ms at p99.

priya: customer says this started after the new tool-router + strict schema validation rollout yesterday (v2.3.1). They have a high qps route (bursty) so any sync per-request validation will amplify tail latency.

jon: confirmed in traces — I pulled a few traces from tracing.prod for req_0ab12c. Router span shows a blocking "schema_validator.validate()" step that sits between request de-serialization and tool dispatch. Sample: 
```
span: router.handle_request
  -> parse_payload (2ms)
  -> schema_validator.validate (230ms)
  -> tool_router.dispatch (5ms)
  -> runtime.execute (80ms)
```
At p99 validation is 400ms+ for complex schemas (arrays of nested objects). The change in cc9b2f1 (PR #4897 by @jon) introduced synchronous full-schema validation and JSONSchema v7 strict checks.

ryan: aha. so two things: 1) synchronous validation in the hot path, 2) larger schemas from structured output (customers ask for complex arrays) — both increase CPU/parse work and hurt tail. We saw a small bump in our canary but not this much (canary qps wasn't as bursty).

maia: customer wants mitigation asap. What's the immediate short-term fix we can apply without full revert?

jon: short-term options (ordered by speed/risk):
1) toggle feature-flag to disable strict schema validation for high-QPS customers/routes (fast, no deploy).
2) enable sampling-based validation: validate 1% of requests (reduces CPU) — requires flag + small config change.
3) run validation async: accept request, dispatch tool, validate in background and if validation fails we emit telemetry + do compensating flow (more work). Needs small patch but lower risk than full revert.
4) revert to previous router image that skips full-schema checks (safe but will remove protections).

priya: can we do 1) now for AcmeProd? how do I toggle?

jon: yes. ops flag is `router.enable_strict_schema`. In console -> infra -> feature-flags -> filter by customer_id=acme-prod -> set to false. CLI: `rb feature-flag set router.enable_strict_schema false --target acme-prod` (this hits rollout service, takes ~30s to propagate). I'll stay on call while you flip it.

maia: doing it now. flipping flag...

priya: flipped and verified 200 OK from rollout service.

ops-bot: Feature flag router.enable_strict_schema set to false for acme-prod by priya at 2025-06-09T11:20:12Z.

jon: monitoring. pulling metrics...

maia: early signs: p99 dropped from 720ms -> 180ms in the next 2m window for that route. customer reports fewer timeouts. :relieved:

ryan: good. follow-up next steps:
- short term (owner: jon): keep flag off for acme-prod and any other high-QPS customers that reported regressions. Backfill telemetry to see validation_fail_rate when disabled.
- mid term (owner: eng-runtime): change validator to be async by default and make strict validation opt-in per route. This means the router dispatch path won't wait on full-schema checks.
- mid term (owner: eng-platform): add sampling and an LRU cache of compiled schemas (we're re-compiling the same schemas per-request right now). Compiled-schema cache should cut validation cpu/time massively.
- long term (owner: devex/eng-ml): provide a lightweight pre-validated schema guide and warn in console when schemas exceed complexity thresholds.

jon: technical notes for mid-term: compiled_schema_cache: TTL=1h, size=2048, use schema fingerprinting (sha1 of normalized schema) as key. Also change validate() to fast-path: if array/object sizes exceed threshold, short-circuit to a sampled async validation. We need to be careful with correctness for customers that require synchronous guarantees — that's why make it opt-in per-route.

priya: customer asked for formal RCA and when we'll re-enable strict checks. SLA liaison requested a timeline.

maia: tentative timeline: 
- today: feature-flag disable per-customer + monitor (done).
- +48h: roll sampling + compiled-cache patch to canary (jon + eng-runtime).
- +7d: async-validation change and opt-in console UI (ryan + eng-platform + devex).

jon: I'll open a follow-up PR that: (a) adds compiled-schema cache, (b) introduces `validate_async` hook, (c) feature-flag gating for strict mode. PR will reference cc9b2f1 revert plan if we need it.

maia: please drop the PR link here and tag me. Priya — can you send the customer a short update: root cause = synchronous full-schema validation added in v2.3.1 + bursty complex schemas -> p99 tail latency. mitigation applied (feature-flag disabled) and we are shipping cache+sampling as next step.

priya: will do, sending message now.

jon: one more data request (for postmortem): please export a sample set of requests (headers + request size + schema fingerprint + validation.time_ms) for the 1h window around the incident. Also include trace ids for top 10 slowest. This will help tune sampling thresholds.

maia: noted — I'll pull logs and attach to the incident ticket INC-2025-208.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2025-208 created by maia: "p99 regression on function router for acme-prod due to sync schema validation". Priority: P1.

ryan: OK. we should also add a short-term perf test to catch this in future canaries: synth load with bursts and representative complex schemas. Add to canary test harness (owner: eng-sre).

maia: thanks everyone — current state: mitigation applied, customer notified, monitoring in place. We'll reconvene once jon posts the PR and we have telemetry from the canary.

jon: PR draft will be up in ~3h. tagging @maia @ryan.

priya: thanks team. I'll keep the customer updated hourly until stable.
